evidence.quote: Bulk (Ti55V30Zr15)95Al5 alloy ingots were produced by arc-melting a mixture high purity of raw materials (over 99.9 wt. %) under an Ar atmosphere. In order to prevent oxidization and promote homogeneity, a high-purity Ti-getter was used to absorb residual oxygen, and each ingot was flipped and re-melted for eight times.
The as-cast bulk samples were processed via homogenization at 1200 ◦C or 1000 ◦C for 2 h followed by water quenching (denoted as 1200- or 1000-MPEA), respectively.
The as-cast bulk samples were processed via homogenization at 1200 ◦C or 1000 ◦C for 2 h followed by water quenching (denoted as 1200- or 1000-MPEA), respectively.

After homogenization, cold rolling with a reduction in thickness of 50 to 90 % was performed (denoted as CR-X hereafter, e.g., X = 90). The 1200-MPEA CR-80 specimens with the most excellent mechanical properties is referred to as structurally heterogeneous nanostructured alloy, HNA-S.
Finally, portions of the HNA-S specimens were aged at 400 ◦C for 40 min, to produce what we term “structurally and chemically heterogeneous nanostructured alloy”, i.e., HNA-(S + C).
